$comment: R1840/R1842 — THE OPTION SURFACE THE TOOL IS AN EDITOR FOR, SOURCED RATHER
THAN DECLARED.
R1690 built `hello-node-lab::settings::schema` and registered the defect in
the same breath: the surface the reach meter divides by was written BY HAND
IN THE SAME CRATE AS THE SCREEN UNDER TEST. That is the shape the sibling
specification pins already refuse (`ls docs/analyzer-*-spec.json`, and ask
the directory rather than trusting a number written here — the first draft
of this line said THREE and there were twelve) — a specification written by
the same hand in the same edit as its subject means a conformance check is
asking the subject for the answer — and the coverage meter made it worse
than usual, because the drift has a DIRECTION: a surface that falls behind
its target shrinks the denominator, so the number goes UP. Drift reads as
progress.
This file is that surface, taken from outside the crate.
★★★★★ R1842 — WHICH LIST IN THE REFERENCE, AND WHY THE FIRST CHOICE WAS
THE WRONG ONE. R1840 extracted this from the reference's node-inspector
field CATALOGUE — the list of keys its inspector offers to add. Re-read at
R1842, the reference says in its own words what that list is: the
frequently-used ones put in front, and NOT the boundary of the
configuration. It is the reference's PALETTE. Measuring a palette against a
palette is the same defect this pin exists to remove, one level up: the
numerator was standing in for the denominator, and the figure that produced
was the flattering one.
The reference carries the boundary separately, and says where it got it:
the target prints its whole configuration when it starts, and the reference
read that dump. It keeps the result as its own schema and uses it as the
ONLY gate against a mistyped key — because the target answers an unknown
key with a warning and starts anyway. That list is what this file now
holds, and it is larger than the catalogue by more than a factor of two.
THE DERIVATION POINT, which is the half R1690 said was missing. Two levels,
both recorded: the target declares the surface as it starts and the
reference read it there; the reference additionally cites the target's own
default configuration document by line range beside the fields those lines
authorise, ten times, and cites the target's source forty-six times in all.
THE SHAPES ARE THE SOURCE'S TOO, NOW — coarsely. The reference types each
leaf from the same dump's default values, and for the leaves whose default
is null it takes the type from the target's own signatures instead, citing
them. Its words are coarse (`array`, `bool`, `number`, `object`, `string`)
and three leaves it cannot type at all, which it SAYS rather than guesses —
so `unknown` is carried here as a shape rather than quietly defaulted.
This tree's `FieldType` is finer: a formatted address, a bounded integer, a
unique identifier. Those refinements stay the screen's and are applied per
path in `settings.rs`. What moves here is the POPULATION, which is the
thing a meter divides by.
★ WHY THE COARSE TYPE IS NOT DECORATION: the reference records that an
unknown KEY is survivable and a wrong TYPE is not — the target refuses to
finish starting. So a shape word here is a start-up gate, not a preference.

$substituted.why: the reference's vocabulary is confidential; structure and behaviour are reproduced, words are not
$substituted.how: path stems are substituted one-for-one, following the conventions `settings.rs` already used, so a path here and the same path there differ only in the substituted stem
$substituted.note: the neutral side is recorded and the original side deliberately is not — writing the mapping down here would publish exactly what the substitution exists to withhold
$substituted.$one_stem_changed_at_r1842: one of R1840's eight neutral stems COLLIDED once the whole surface was present: it mapped a section of the source onto a word the source also uses for a leaf of its own, and a leaf that is the prefix of another leaf is a document that cannot exist — `ConfigSchema::new` refuses it by name. The collision was unreachable while only the catalogue was here, because the catalogue holds one of the two and not the other. That is the ninth stem's reason for existing

dynamic_roots.$why: the reference declares one root whose children are not in the schema at all — the names under it are chosen by whoever installs something, so any path below it is valid and none of them can be enumerated. Recorded rather than expanded: this tree's `ConfigSchema` has no vocabulary for a root like that, so a path under it is neither a leaf we are missing nor a key the target refuses, and a census unable to say so would report it as one or the other forever

not_config.$why: the reference marks these with a scope word of its own: they are traffic parameters and placement axes with no key in the target. Recorded rather than dropped, because a path missing from the surface and a path the target has no key for are different facts, and a census that could not tell them apart would report the second as a gap forever

$also_a_path.why: the reference's split is per ROW, not per name: a row is configuration or it is not, and the same word can be both on two different rows. `id` is the target's own identity path on an infrastructure row AND the run-only argument a traffic program takes.
